content: Directions for Items 704 to 706: A real-valued function $f(x)$ of a real variable $x$ is said to be periodic if there is a strictly positive real number $p$ such that $f(x+p)=f(x)$ for every $x$. The smallest $p$ satisfying the above property is called the period of $f$.
